lovelace.name: The Notes by A.A.L.
lovelace.hook: The first published computer program appeared in 1843, for a machine that has never been built. Its author saw what it meant. Nobody else did for a century.

lovelace.name: Boolean algebra
lovelace.hook: In 1854, a shoemaker's son with no degree wrote a book on how humans think. Minds never ran on it. Every machine you own does instead.

remarks.name: John Crowley
remarks.text: Claude Shannon's master's thesis in 1938 was published, it gave a rigorous foundation to field of circuit design digital logic by applying Boolean algebra to circuit simplification. The paper has been called the most influential and important master's thesis ever.

lovelace.name: Shannon's thesis
lovelace.hook: In 1937, a 21-year-old's MIT master's thesis showed how electrical switches could perform logic. Every digital device since runs on that idea.

wright.name: The 1901 wind tunnel
wright.hook: In 1901, every lift calculation on Earth used a constant from the 1700s. Two bicycle mechanics checked it. It was off by fifty percent.

remarks.name: Bill Platt
remarks.title: Naval Architect
remarks.text: The strangest thing about the Wrights was their transition from being the very essence of science, to being fearful hoarders and patent and lawsuit obsessed tycoons. They stopped inventing. And aeronautics passed them by.

remarks.name: Brian Berthold
remarks.text: Where are those naysayers complaining about too small, too slow, wrong Reynolds number??? Good thing they weren't around then.
remarks.note: Consent conditional (LinkedIn, Jul 2026): feature on the site only; do not use this comment to train AI.

remarks.name: Matias Soto
remarks.title: PhD
remarks.text: The Wright brothers are constantly referred as bicycle mechanics, as if that meant they were uneducated or ignorant. History shows they were avid readers and students of science and mathematics, and constantly experimented with high tech. Through that process they became the leading experts in their field.
remarks.note: Attribution caveat (LinkedIn, Jul 2026): credit as relaying, not as the original source of the facts.

petroski.name: Tacoma Narrows Bridge
petroski.hook: In 1940 a four-month-old bridge tore itself apart in a 42 mph wind. It was strong enough. Nobody had asked whether it was stiff enough.

petroski.name: Ronan Point
petroski.hook: In 1968 a gas stove flexed one wall panel out of a new 22-storey tower. A whole corner fell to the ground, flat by flat.

hammurabi.name: British Airtours Flight 28M
hammurabi.hook: In 1985, 55 people died feet from an exit they could not reach. The gap beside the overwing door was built to the width of the rule, not the width of a person.

barenyi.name: The crumple zone
barenyi.hook: In 1951 Bela Barenyi patented a car built to destroy itself. Rigid in the middle, folding at the ends, on purpose. Patent DBP 854157 is in every car you have ridden since.

tipper.name: Liberty ships
tipper.hook: In January 1943 the tanker Schenectady cracked nearly in two at her dock, in calm water. The welds held. The steel turned brittle in the cold.

tipper.name: NASA 3D-printed chamber
tipper.hook: In 2021 a printed rocket chamber failed nine seconds into a burn. The build logs looked clean. The crack ran exactly along the line where the printer had paused.

roebling.name: Bazalgette's London sewers
roebling.hook: IN 1858, THE GREAT STINK DROVE PARLIAMENT TO DEBATE LEAVING LONDON. THE ENGINEER HIRED TO KILL THE SMELL MADE EVERY PIPE TWICE AS WIDE, AND STOPPED CHOLERA WITHOUT MEANING TO.

roebling.name: Brooklyn Bridge
roebling.hook: THE BROOKLYN BRIDGE'S CABLES CONTAIN 221 TONS OF WIRE THAT FAILED INSPECTION. THE ENGINEER WHO CAUGHT THE FRAUD COULDN'T REMOVE IT. IT'S STILL THERE.

roebling.name: Quebec Bridge
roebling.hook: THE ORDER TO STOP WORK ON THE QUEBEC BRIDGE REACHED THE COMPANY AT 1:15 PM. NOBODY RELAYED IT TO THE SITE. NEAR 5:30 THE BRIDGE FELL, KILLING 75 MEN.

sutter.name: de Havilland Comet 1
sutter.hook: In 1952 the world's first jet airliner entered service. Then it began falling out of the sky, and the cause was a crack no bigger than a fingernail at the corner of a window.

sutter.name: Boeing 747
sutter.hook: In 1965 Boeing bet the company on a jet twice the size of anything flying and gave Joe Sutter 29 months to design it. The team that built it called themselves the Incredibles.

carnot.name: Rudolf Diesel's engine
carnot.hook: In 1897 Rudolf Diesel ran an engine that beat steam on efficiency and could burn almost any fuel, peanut oil included. He vanished off a ship 16 years later.

noyce.name: The point-contact transistor
noyce.hook: In December 1947 Bell Labs officials heard a voice amplified through a plastic triangle, a strip of gold foil, and a slab of germanium. The vacuum-tube era was finished.

noyce.name: The Traitorous Eight and the planar process
noyce.hook: The company that printed the first manufacturable microchip was founded on ten signed one-dollar bills and $500 a man. Its founders' old boss called them traitors.

noyce.name: TSMC and the pure-play foundry (Part 2)
noyce.hook: Morris Chang failed his MIT doctorate, spent 25 years at Texas Instruments, and in 1987 built a factory that would only make other companies' chips. It now makes nearly all the advanced ones.

noyce.name: NVIDIA RIVA 128 (Part 1)
noyce.hook: In 1996 NVIDIA had one month of payroll left. It designed its next chip entirely in software, sent it straight to first silicon, and would have died if that silicon failed. It did not.

noyce.name: ASML and EUV lithography (Part 3)
noyce.hook: To print the smallest chips, ASML fires a laser at 50,000 droplets of molten tin every second, turning each into a plasma nearly 40 times hotter than the Sun's surface, all to make a single wavelength of light no lens can bend.

noyce.name: AlexNet and the CUDA bet (Part 4)
noyce.hook: The graphics cards that trained the first modern AI in 2012 could do it only because of a bet NVIDIA made in 2006, six years before anyone needed it.
